subject.title: fix(gateway): force exit on zombie shutdown + 503 healthz during shutdown

question: Should Gateway adopt this default recovery contract: force `process.exit(0)` five seconds after clean non-restart shutdown and make supervised lock recovery depend on `/healthz?strict=1` returning 200 only?
rationale: The code path is coherent and tested, but the remaining choice changes process-supervision and operator behavior in a way automation cannot approve from source alone.

options.title: Accept the recovery contract
options.body: Land this branch with the current default watchdog timeout, strict internal probe, and public `/healthz` compatibility.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Require a smaller policy surface, such as a different timeout/default or no new env knob, before accepting the fix.

options.title: Reject this layer
options.body: Close or replace the branch if maintainers want only the original SIGKILL/root-cause path fixed and no second-order forced-exit defense.

recommendation.title: Accept the recovery contract
recommendation.body: Land this branch with the current default watchdog timeout, strict internal probe, and public `/healthz` compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Gateway lifecycle, process supervision, and operator defaults, and this handle has the strongest recent cross-surface ownership signal.
